title: Decision: which iOS request path carries POST /v1/events and PATCH /v1/installation
description: Identify the exact client(s)/methods to hook for outgoing injection and incoming interception so the server algorithm actually receives sync params.
design: JS injects _syncUserId/_syncDeviceId/_syncInstallationId/_syncVisitorId + _SOURCESync.* on POST /events and PATCH /installation, and intercepts those responses plus _serverTime. iOS candidates: events via WPMeasurementsApiClient (measurements-api.wonderpush.com) and/or WPAPIClient (WonderPushConcreteAPI.m:160-167); PATCH /installation via WPJsonSyncInstallation.m:263-285 -> WonderPush.requestForUser. Injection point: WPBaseAPIClient.decorateRequestParams (WPAPIClient.m:132). Interception point: WPRequest.handler / WPBaseAPIClient.executeRequest.
acceptance_criteria: Confirmed list of client+method hook points for both endpoints, both directions.
notes: RESOLVED. Findings: POST /events is sent by (a) trackEvent path -> WPAPIClient/WPAnonymousAPIClient (WonderPushConcreteAPI.m:247,259) and (b) countEvent path -> WPMeasurementsApiClient (WonderPushConcreteAPI.m:166). PATCH /installation -> WPAPIClient via WonderPush.requestForUser (from WPJsonSyncInstallation.m). DECISION: cover BOTH carriers in v1. Main+anonymous path hooks centrally in WPBaseAPIClient (decorateRequestParams WPAPIClient.m:131 outgoing; executeRequest success handler parsing responseJSON incoming). Measurements path is a different lineage (WPBasicApiClient) decorating a body STRING (WPMeasurementsApiClient.m:32 decorateRequestBody:userId:) -> separate injection + response parse, tracked as its own issue.
close_reason: Decided: hook WPBaseAPIClient (main+anon) AND WPMeasurementsApiClient (body-string) in v1.

title: Plug synced contact data into the segmentation engine
description: Make the synced contact object (sdk-sync contact source) readable by the WPSP segmentation engine so popups/in-app messages can segment on contact attributes. Mirrors the JS SDK (commit 4ef542f 'Plug synced contact data into in-app/popup segmentation'). contact is a DISTINCT namespace from user and installation: an installation custom field named firstName must NOT satisfy a contact criterion, and a null/absent contact makes contact criteria non-match.
design: JS reference: Segmenter gets contactProperties (segmenter.ts ctor ~56-71); ContactVisitor resolves contact.* field paths into the contact JSON (segmenter.ts 573-590); join point instantiates ContactVisitor (segmenter.ts 285-297); in-app eval fetches Sync.getSourceData('contact') and passes it to the Segmenter (main.ts 262-264, 310-320); automatic-actions.ts does the same. Field paths: contact.firstName, contact.attributes.PLAN (dot notation, null-safe, empty-array on miss). iOS injection: (1) extend WPSPSegmenterData (WPSPSegmenter.h ~27-37) with a contact NSDictionary and thread it through initWithInstallation:...; (2) WPSPSegmenterData.forCurrentUser (WPSPSegmenter.m 48-66) fetches the synced contact from the WPSyncContactSource read accessor (.19) and includes it; (3) add a dedicated contact namespace: register @"contact" in WPSPDefaultCriterionNodeParser init (~line 42) with a parseContact mirroring parseUser (WPSPDefaultCriterionNodeParser.m 160-180), and resolve it via WPSPContactSource + visitContactSource (or the existing-but-unused WPSPUserSource — but keep contact and user SEPARATE per JS); (4) the field resolution reuses the visitFieldSource dictionary-walk (WPSPSegmenter.m 509-554). Popup segment eval already builds WPSPSegmenterData.forCurrentUser (WPIAMMessageClientCache.m 169-205), so it picks up contact for free once wired.
acceptance_criteria: A segment {contact:{.firstName:{eq:Alice}}} matches iff the synced contact has firstName Alice; an installation custom field firstName does NOT satisfy it; no synced contact -> non-match. Nested contact.attributes.X works. WPSPSegmenterTests cover contact criteria.
notes:
User-source (.21) segmentation is the symmetric follow-up (JS wired both contact and user, bd 4cq): add a user namespace the same way. Out of scope here; tracked alongside the user source .21.
DONE. Added a  segmentation namespace, distinct from installation/user (mirrors JS): WPSPContactSource (data source) + visitContactSource + WPSPContactVisitor (resolves fields against data.contact) + a contact branch in visitJoinCriterionNode; parser registers @"contact" -> parseContact (installation-root -> WPSPJoinCriterionNode). WPSPSegmenterData gains a readwrite contact property; forCurrentUser injects it from [WPSyncManager dataForSource:@"contact"] (nil when sync off). 4 XCTest (contact field match; contact != installation; nested contact.attributes; installation namespace unaffected) + existing 35 WPSPSegmenterTests still green.
close_reason: contact segmentation namespace wired (source/visitor/parser/join + data injection); 4 tests + no regression in 35 existing segmenter tests.

title: WPSync orchestrator singleton + lifecycle
description: Tie the glue together behind a single coordinator with source registration.
design: Port sync.js: registerSource(name,plugin), identifiers(), prepareOutgoingParams, consumeIncomingResponse, fetch(source), checkMaxAgeForcing after each response. Initialize on SDK init; track current profile via WPConfiguration userId/deviceId/installationId; handle identifier-change reset (reset to empty + refetch within the same profile slot).
acceptance_criteria: Sources register; opportunistic + explicit + max-age forcing wired end-to-end.
notes:
REQUIREMENTS from code review (deferred-here findings the orchestrator must satisfy):
(D) Logout/clearStorage race: WPConfiguration.clearStorageKeepUserConsent: wipes __wonderpush_* keys (incl. __wonderpush_syncStatePerProfile) under WPConfiguration's lock, while WPSyncStateStore writes under its own singleton lock — disjoint lock domains over the same NSUserDefaults. The orchestrator MUST quiesce sync on userId-change/logout/clearStorage: stop/await in-flight fetches and not write sync state after a clear, so a logged-out device cannot re-persist the prior profile's cursors.
(E) load->process->save atomicity: WPSyncStateStore makes each load and each save individually atomic but NOT the read-modify-write spanning a fetch/response. The orchestrator MUST hold the per-source processing mutex (WPSyncMutex mutexNamed:'sync:proc:'+source, .17) across the WHOLE load->processSourceBlock->save cycle so concurrent opportunistic+explicit updates to the same source don't lose a cursor advance. Use the token-based tryLock/unlock:.
(F) deviceId invariant: WPSyncStateStore.storageKeyForSource collapses nil/empty deviceId to '' (slot collision). The orchestrator MUST only call load/save with a real (non-empty) deviceId — deviceId is established at SDK init; guard/skip sync before it exists.
MORE review requirements (from the .16 fetch-loop review):
(5/E reinforced) WPSyncFetcher's success path does load->set count=0->save as two separate store calls, which can clobber the incoming interceptor's concurrent lastVersion/lastReadDate advance (last-writer-wins on the whole record). The orchestrator MUST run the fetch's count-reset and the response processing under the SAME per-source processing mutex (sync:proc:<source>) so they don't interleave — same coordination already required for opportunistic-vs-explicit updates.
(8) Efficiency: that success path also re-loads the whole NSUserDefaults blob just to flip the failure counter. When .18 unifies the count-reset into the processing cycle (under the mutex above), fold the counter reset into the same read-modify-write the interceptor already does, rather than a second load+save.
Also: when wiring the real transport adapter, it MUST always invoke the fetcher's completion (success OR failure, incl. on timeout) so the mutex is released promptly; the mutex TTL (mutexTtlMs) is only the backstop for a dropped callback.
PROGRESS: orchestrator CORE done + tested (WPSync.{h,m}). registerSource:plugin: (WPSyncSourcePlugin protocol: optional clearState/applyData:/applyDelta:); prepareOutgoingParamsForPath:method: (gates on opportunistic classify + kill switch + deviceId invariant, gathers per-source state -> WPSyncOutgoing); consumeIncomingResponseForPath:method:response: (classify -> per registered source for opportunistic / extractExplicitBlock for explicit -> processSource (per-source @synchronized span: load->processSourceBlock->executeDecision) -> save state + plug-in callbacks clearState/applyData/applyDelta + fire-and-forget fetch via id<WPSyncFetching> -> checkMaxAgeForcing); dataForSource: for segmentation/popup engines. DI: stateStore + fetcher injected; identifiers/knobs/now via block providers. 12 XCTest cases. Full sync suite 121 green.
REMAINING (still in_progress): (a) real WPAPIClient/WPMeasurementsApiClient transport adapter (id<WPSyncFetchTransport>) + GET wiring; (b) the request hooks .14 (decorateRequestParams -> prepareOutgoingParams) and .15 (executeRequest success -> consumeIncomingResponse); (c) SDK-init lifecycle (instantiate WPSync, wire identifiers from WPConfiguration, knobs from WPSyncKnobsProvider); (d) logout/clearStorage quiesce; (e) the fetcher success count-reset must be ordered under/after response processing (run the interceptor before the transport completion) to avoid the cursor-clobber race.
PROGRESS: real transport adapter done (WPSyncAPITransport, testable). Conforms to WPSyncFetchTransport; issues the explicit-fetch GET via an INJECTED sender block (so it's unit-tested without the live client) and maps the response to success=(error==nil); the response body is applied by the incoming interceptor (.15). Threaded userId through WPSyncFetchTransport so the GET uses the fetch's captured profile (not a re-read). 2 XCTest. At SDK init the sender will be wired to WonderPush.requestForUser:method:@"GET":resource:params:handler:. Full sync suite 127 green.
STILL REMAINING on .18 (the un-unit-testable core-path wiring; needs .20 integration tests on a machine that can run the example app): (a) the WPBaseAPIClient request hooks — .14 decorateRequestParams -> prepareOutgoingParams, .15 executeRequest success -> consumeIncomingResponse (+ .25 Measurements); (b) SDK-init lifecycle: instantiate WPSync (+ WPSyncFetcher + WPSyncAPITransport + WPSyncStateStore.defaultStore + WPSyncKnobsProvider), wire identifiersProvider from WPConfiguration (userId/deviceId/installationId), register WPSyncContactSource; (c) logout/clearStorage quiesce.
DONE. WPSyncManager assembles the stack (WPSyncStateStore.defaultStore + WPSyncAPITransport + WPSyncFetcher + WPSync + WPSyncContactSource), caches effective knobs from remote config (WPSyncKnobsProvider, refreshed on WPRemoteConfigUpdatedNotification), and installs the WPSync observer via WPSyncHook ONLY when remote-config syncEnabled is true (default off -> whole channel inert). WonderPush.m refreshSyncManager supplies identifiersProvider (userId/deviceId/installationId from WonderPush) + the request sender (WonderPush.requestForUser GET); called from the existing remote-config-updated observer. Compile-verified (framework + WonderPush.m build). Live activation behavior verified by .20 integration tests; logout quiesce handled by the syncEnabled gate + identifiers re-read per request (deviceId invariant).
close_reason: Lifecycle assembly done + gated off; all hook deps (.14/.15/.25) closed.

title: Per-source mutex + processing serialization
description: Serialize fetches and response processing per source on a single process.
design: JS uses named cross-tab mutexes with TTL (sync:SOURCE and sync:proc:SOURCE). iOS single-process: per-source serial dispatch queue or NSLock + in-flight guard for both fetch and load->process->save cycles. Crash-safety across launches via persisted lastFetchAttemptedDate rather than TTL.
acceptance_criteria: No interleaving of process cycles; no parallel fetch per source.
notes: DONE. WPSyncMutex.{h,m}: named, process-wide-shared, non-blocking tryLock/unlock; cross-thread safe (internal NSLock guard around a held flag, so unlock can run on the network-completion thread). No TTL (single process; crash resets in-memory locks; cross-launch safety is the persisted lastFetchAttemptedDate guard in the fetch loop). 4 XCTest cases: exclusivity/reacquire, per-name shared singletons, independent names, cross-thread unlock. The fetch loop (.16) uses mutexNamed:'sync:'+source; the orchestrator (.18) will use mutexNamed:'sync:proc:'+source to serialize the load->process->save cycle. TEST SUCCEEDED.
close_reason: Per-source mutex primitive implemented (named non-blocking cross-thread try-lock), 4 tests pass; processing-cycle serialization uses it from .18.

title: Explicit fetch scheduling + backoff (WPSyncFetcher)
description: Implement the explicit GET fetch loop with backoff, debounce, and rate-limit.
design: GET /contact|/user|/installation|/popups|/inbox via WPAPIClient. Port sync.js fetch loop (algorithm.md:245-257): weak-signal debounce, per-source rate-limit floor (all triggers), acquire mutex, stamp lastFetchAttemptedDate, increment fail count, backoff sleep via dispatch_after, on success reset count + process response, on failure leave count, release mutex.
acceptance_criteria: Backoff/retry/rate-limit honored; single in-flight fetch per source.
notes: DONE. WPSyncFetcher.{h,m}: ports the Sync.fetch/runFetchWithMutexHeld loop (algorithm.md:245-257). Steps: weak-signal debounce + per-source rate-limit guards -> per-source WPSyncMutex tryLock ('sync:'+source, token-based) -> stamp lastFetchAttemptedDate + increment failure count + persist BEFORE the call -> backoff sleep -> GET via injected id<WPSyncFetchTransport> -> on HTTP success reload+reset count+save (response body itself is applied by the incoming interceptor .15), on failure leave count -> always release mutex via the matched token. Network + clock + scheduler + random are injected for deterministic isolation. Path derived via WPSyncExplicitPathForSource; params via buildExplicitFetchParams. 10 XCTest cases (unknown-source/weak/rate-limit/mutex-busy aborts, stamp+GET+params, backoff delay 0 and 8000, success-resets vs failure-leaves count, mutex released). Full sync suite 107 green. OUT OF SCOPE (deferred): multi-object paging continuation = block-acquire of the mutex (.23/.24); the real WPAPIClient transport adapter + wiring into the orchestrator (.18).
close_reason: Explicit fetch loop (guards/mutex/backoff/bookkeeping) implemented with DI, 10 tests pass; real transport adapter wired in .18.

title: Outgoing param injection (WPSyncOutgoing) + request-build hook
description: Inject identifiers and per-source sync cursor onto opportunistic requests. Must work for BOTH outgoing carriers: the SDK API (WPBaseAPIClient -> WPAPIClient / WPAnonymousAPIClient, for POST /events and PATCH /installation) AND the Measurements API (WPMeasurementsApiClient, for the countEvent POST /events path). The same _sync* identifiers and _SOURCESync.* cursor must be attached on both, adapted to each client's encoding.
design: Port sync-outgoing.ts buildOutgoingParams + shouldInjectForPath. Add _syncUserId/_syncDeviceId/_syncInstallationId/_syncVisitorId and _SOURCESync.{lastSyncDate,lastSyncMeta(JSON),lastVersion,lastVersionId,lastReadDate} on POST /events and PATCH /installation; omit null fields. Hook at the path determined by D2 (e.g. WPBaseAPIClient.decorateRequestParams). Gate on opportunisticInjectionEnabled.
acceptance_criteria: Both endpoints carry correct params; disabled when kill-switch off.
notes:
Scope per i2x.2: this issue covers the main+anonymous WPBaseAPIClient path; the WPMeasurementsApiClient body-string path is handled in wonderpush-ios-sdk-i2x.25.
SCOPE UPDATE (per user): .14 now owns the requirement for BOTH the SDK API and the Measurements API carriers (supersedes the earlier note that scoped this to WPBaseAPIClient only). The Measurements API uses a different lineage (WPBasicApiClient, body-string via decorateRequestBody:userId:) so its encoding differs. Open question: fold .25 into .14, or keep .25 as the measurements-specific implementation sub-task under this requirement?
PARTIAL: WPSyncOutgoing.{h,m} pure builder done + tested (shouldInjectForPath host-agnostic for /events & /installation incl. Measurements API; buildOutgoingParamsWithIdentifiers:statePerSource: emits _sync<Id> + _<source>Sync.* keys, JSON-encoded lastSyncMeta, omits nil meta/versionId, NEVER contactId). 6 XCTest cases. REMAINING (kept in_progress): the request-layer HOOK that gathers current identifiers + registered-source state and merges buildOutgoingParams onto outgoing requests on BOTH WPBaseAPIClient (decorateRequestParams) and WPMeasurementsApiClient — that needs the orchestrator's source registry + identifiers + state store, so it lands with .18. Deferred deliberately as SDK-core integration for the next review batch.
Request-build hook DONE (SDK API path): WPBaseAPIClient.decorateRequestParams now merges sync params from the installed WPSyncRequestObserver (WPAPIClient.m), via the WPSyncHook seam — nil-guarded so it's INERT until SDK-init installs the observer (no behavior change otherwise), and never overwrites existing keys. Compile-verified (framework builds, 130 tests green incl. existing client tests). The pure builder (WPSyncOutgoing) + this hook cover the SDK API; Measurements API injection is .25. Live behavior verified by .20 integration tests.
close_reason: Outgoing builder + decorateRequestParams hook done; observer installed by .18 lifecycle (gated).

title: Incoming response interceptor -> processor
description: Intercept API responses and feed sync blocks to the processor.
design: Port sync-incoming-wrap.ts behavior. Wrap response handling in WPBaseAPIClient.executeRequest / WPRequest.handler to read _serverTime and _SOURCESync (opportunistic) or top-level fields (explicit), classifyResponse, run processSourceBlock, persist newState, run plugin callbacks (applyData/applyDelta/clearState), then trigger fetch + checkMaxAgeForcing. Fire-and-forget; never block the original handler.
acceptance_criteria: Opportunistic and explicit responses update state and fire follow-up fetches correctly.
notes:
Scope per i2x.2: this issue covers the main+anonymous WPBaseAPIClient path; the WPMeasurementsApiClient response parse is handled in wonderpush-ios-sdk-i2x.25.
Incoming hook DONE (SDK API path): WPBaseAPIClient.executeRequest success handler now calls the installed WPSyncRequestObserver's consumeIncomingResponseForPath:method:response: with the parsed responseJSON (WPAPIClient.m), via the WPSyncHook seam — nil-guarded/inert until SDK-init installs the observer; best-effort (WPSync guards with @try/@catch). Compile-verified (130 tests green). Measurements-client interception is .25. Live behavior verified by .20.
close_reason: executeRequest success -> consumeIncomingResponse hook done; observer installed by .18.

notes: DONE. WPSyncKnobsProvider.{h,m}: +knobsFromRemoteConfig: (pure; reads config.data, merges sync* over DEFAULT_KNOBS via WPSyncKnobs mergeKnobsFromDefaults:remoteConfig:, nil config -> defaults) and -readKnobs: (reads WPRemoteConfigManager.read: and merges; error/no-config -> defaults). 7 XCTest: nil/empty -> defaults, overrides applied, kill-switch (only @NO disables), unrelated config keys ignored, + async readKnobs over a real WPRemoteConfigManager with inline mock fetcher/storage (fetched config merged; nil -> defaults). TEST SUCCEEDED.

title: WPSyncStateStore persistence (NSUserDefaults, per source x profile)
description: Persist per-source per-profile sync state across launches and user switches.
design: Port sync-state.ts SyncState + storageKey scoped by (source,userId,deviceId). iOS: new WPConfiguration key e.g. __wonderpush_syncStatePerSourcePerUserId, JSON serialized like WPJsonSyncInstallation.m:214-220. load/save/emptyState; retain non-current profile slots so switching back avoids refetch; deviceId from WPConfiguration.deviceId.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip persistence test; profile switch retains and restores slots.
notes: DONE. WPSyncStateStore.{h,m}: per-(source,userId,deviceId) persistence. storageKeyForSource:userId:deviceId: -> 'sync:<source>:<userId||"">:<deviceId>'. defaultStore uses standardUserDefaults; initWithUserDefaults: injectable for tests. Backing blob is a single JSON-as-NSData dict {storageKey: stateDict} under __wonderpush_syncStatePerProfile, @synchronized read-modify-write. JSON (not raw NSDictionary) is REQUIRED because SyncSourceState carries NSNull for null fields, which NSUserDefaults cannot store directly; JSON null<->nil round-trips correctly. Non-current profiles retained (unsetUserId reuse). 6 XCTest cases on an isolated suite: key format, empty default, null round-trip, persistence across instances (relaunch), profile+source+device isolation/retention. TEST SUCCEEDED.
close_reason: Per-source/profile NSUserDefaults persistence implemented, wired, 6 tests pass.

title: Decision: multi-object (popups/inbox) local store, merge and entry caps model
description: Decide list storage shape and merge implementation for multi-object sources before implementing them.
design: Multi-object sources store a single server-merged list (never split per identifier), apply delta (array of full objects), cap by maxPopupsEntries/maxInboxEntries, order by updateDate desc then id, and accept device-targeted duplication across profiles (algorithm.md:35-51, 136-143, 312-324). Decide NSUserDefaults JSON list shape and dedupe/merge utility. May be deferred.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision covering storage shape, merge, caps, ordering.
notes: RESOLVED (deferrable design). Store one JSON array per (source, profile) in a new WPConfiguration NSUserDefaults key (e.g. __wonderpush_syncListPerSourcePerUserId). Apply delta as array of full objects keyed by id; cap at maxPopupsEntries/maxInboxEntries; order by updateDate desc then id desc (compareVersionId); keep soft-delete tombstones until expiration and filter them on read. Single server-merged list only; never split per identifier; accept device-targeted duplication across profiles. Implemented in S_POP/S_INBOX.
close_reason: Decided: single capped JSON array per source/profile in NSUserDefaults; delta-by-id; tombstones filtered on read.

title: Merge synced popups into the in-app message engine
description: Feed the synced per-user popup rules (sdk-sync popups source) into the in-app message engine alongside the global remote-config inAppConfig.campaigns, so targeted/individualized popups display. Mirrors the JS SDK merge in inappmessaging/main.ts (284-298).
design: JS reference: synced popups are PopupItem[] {id, updateDate, status, expirationDate, data: Campaign}; engine filters tombstones (status==deleted) and expired (expirationDate<now), maps to the Campaign payload, then concatenates inAppConfig.campaigns.concat(syncedCampaigns) (remote-config FIRST = precedence, NO dedupe; sources expected disjoint) before evaluating triggers/segment/capping/display (main.ts 252-367). Synced popups carry no segment of their own beyond the Campaign. Capping is LOCAL per device (bookkeeper IndexedDB); the server does NOT send impression counters back - impressions are reported via @INAPP_VIEWED/@INAPP_CLICKED events whose campaignId piggybacks on /events via opportunistic injection. iOS injection: WPIAMMessageClientCache.loadMessagesFromRemoteConfigWithCompletion: (WPIAMMessageClientCache.m 225-244) reads inAppConfig from WPRemoteConfig and parses via WPIAMFetchResponseParser.parseAPIResponseDictionary -> setMessageData:. Extend this to also pull the synced popups list from WPSyncPopupsSource (.23), filter tombstones/expired, parse each Campaign payload into WPIAMMessageDefinition via WPIAMFetchResponseParser, and merge (remote first) before setMessageData: (WPIAMMessageClientCache.m ~48). Re-run the merge on BOTH WPRemoteConfigUpdatedNotification (existing WPIAMDisplayCheckOnFetchDoneNotificationFlow) AND when the synced popups source changes. Capping/impressions stay on the existing WPIAMBookKeeper (UserDefaults); ensure synced-campaign impressions still emit the reporting events so they reach the server.
acceptance_criteria: A synced popup rule for the current user displays on its trigger after a sync, evaluated alongside remote-config campaigns (remote first); tombstoned/expired synced items are excluded; capping/snooze honored via the existing bookkeeper; impression events emitted for synced campaigns. Integration test covers the merged evaluation (a gap in the JS suite).
